subject: English 1st Paper

source.edition: Revised for the year 2026; revised edition October 2025

passagePolicy: Use the specifically cited source section in the NCTB textbook. Full textbook passages and images are not reproduced. Original writing models are not source facts.

activities.instruction: Read the cited source section and choose the best answer. Different dialogues are separate source units.

items.question: According to the opening paragraph of Section B, what are natural cures often made from?
items.explanation: This describes the source’s terminology, not proof of treatment effectiveness.

items.question: Does Section B present herbal remedies as entirely new inventions?

options.B: No; it describes their use in earlier ages
options.C: Yes; no earlier people used them
options.D: It says history does not exist

items.explanation: The paragraph discusses ancient civilisations and practices passed down through generations.

items.question: Which civilisation is named in the historical paragraph?
items.explanation: Egypt is one of the examples named, alongside India, China, Greece and Rome.

items.question: Who is talking to Mr Arman in Section D?
items.explanation: The dialogue labels identify the speakers.

items.question: What does Mr Arman decide to buy in the dialogue?
items.explanation: He chooses the lotion and asks its price. This is a reading fact, not a product recommendation.

activities.instruction: Answer using the cited text. Equivalent accurate wording is acceptable; support interpretations with details.

items.question: What does the first paragraph of Section B say about the history of herbal medicines?
items.modelAnswer: It says that people used herbal medicines in earlier ages and in several ancient civilisations.

items.question: Name the five places listed as examples of ancient civilisations in the paragraph.
items.modelAnswer: The paragraph lists India, China, Greece, Egypt and Rome.

items.question: What does it mean that practices have come down through generations?
items.modelAnswer: It means that people have passed those practices from one generation to the next.

items.question: Does knowing that a remedy is traditional prove that it is safe for everyone?
items.modelAnswer: No. The age or natural origin of a practice alone does not establish safety or effectiveness. A qualified health professional should guide treatment decisions.

items.question: What information does Mr Arman ask for after choosing the lotion?
items.modelAnswer: He asks how much it costs.

activities.instruction: Explain the word in the cited context, or give the requested alternative meaning. Accept suitable equivalent wording.

acceptedAnswers: a way of thinking or feeling about something
successive groups of people at different periods in a family or society

items.request: meaning as a word, not an instruction
acceptedAnswers: formally recommend or order a medicine or treatment as a qualified practitioner
a qualified professional who prepares or supplies medicines and advises on their safe use

activities.instruction: Write a conversation asking a trusted adult for help when you feel unwell. Do not prescribe medicine or a home remedy.

modelAnswer.speaker: Child
modelAnswer.text: I do not feel well. Could you help me?

modelAnswer.speaker: Adult
modelAnswer.text: Of course. Tell me what you are feeling.

modelAnswer.speaker: Child
modelAnswer.text: I have a headache, and I feel tired.

modelAnswer.speaker: Adult
modelAnswer.text: Thank you for telling me. We will arrange appropriate advice and care.

modelAnswer.speaker: Child
modelAnswer.text: Should I take something from the medicine cupboard?

modelAnswer.speaker: Adult
modelAnswer.text: Do not take medicine on your own. Let us ask a qualified health professional.

modelAnswer.speaker: Child
modelAnswer.text: All right. I will stay with you and explain if I feel worse.

modelAnswer.speaker: Adult
modelAnswer.text: Yes. You do not have to manage this alone.

activities.note: Original safety-oriented language model, not a diagnosis or treatment plan. Serious or worsening symptoms need prompt professional assessment.
assessment: Addresses the task with relevant details
Uses a clear sequence and connected sentences
Uses suitable vocabulary and comprehensible grammar
Accept original accurate responses; do not require memorisation

limitations: Initial Draft pool, not exhaustive chapter quotas or a complete model paper.
Teacher review, Drive backup and website registration are separate steps.
Full printed lesson visually read, but this pool deliberately excludes remedy recipes, doses, brand recommendations and claims of guaranteed efficacy or no side effects.
Section E and treatment-oriented tasks require qualified clinical review before any educational reuse; no home-treatment answer key is generated.
The textbook natural/chemical split is not used as a scientific classification: natural substances also contain chemicals.
Question about safety is explicitly critical reading with a safety qualification, not a claimed quote from the textbook.

safetyReview.scope: Treatment claims/recipes/medicine recommendations only; safe historical and lexical comprehension retained.
